item.title: Combinatorial formulas for the multivariate Markov-Krein transform
item.description: arXiv:2610.30155v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we study the Markov--Krein correspondence in both the univariate and multivariate settings. Our main result provides an explicit moment--moment formula expressing the multivariate moments of the inverse Markov--Krein transform in terms of the multivariate moments of the Markov-Krein transform via cyclic interval partitions. We also derive moment--cumulant relations involving classical, Boolean and free cumulants.
item.dc:creator: Julian Zazueta-Obeso

item.title: Commutators in selfless C$^\ast$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.30199v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that if \((A, \tau)\) is a selfless C\(^\ast\)-probability space with \(\tau\) being a faithful trace, then commutators are dense in \(\ker \tau\).
item.dc:creator: Alexander G. Ravnanger

item.title: An Approximate-Diagonal Characterization of Amenable Actions on C*Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.30821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce relative $h$-diagonals for crossed products $A\rtimes_{\alpha}\Gamma$ by discrete groups, which are positive-form approximate diagonals in the Haagerup tensor product taken relative to $A$. We show that $\alpha$ is amenable if and only if $A\rtimes_{\alpha}\Gamma$ admits a relative $h$-diagonal, an analogue of Johnson's theorem for $L^{1}(G)$.
item.dc:creator: Zhengyu Fu

item.title: Failure of noncommutative Rota's theorem with $L\log L$ endpoint
item.description: arXiv:2610.31560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a factorizable Markov map $T$ on a hyperfinite finite von Neumann algebra and a positive element $x\in L\log L$ for which the sequence $T^n(T^*)^n x$ does not converge bilaterally almost uniformly. This answers a question of Anantharaman-Delaroche \cite{AD2006}.
item.dc:creator: Hiranmoy Ghorui, Suman Mondal, Samya Kumar Ray

item.title: Finite zero products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols
item.description: arXiv:2610.30209v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study finite products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols on the Fock space over the complex plane. If every symbol has the form $f+\overline g$, where $f$ and $g$ are entire functions of exponential type, we prove that a finite product vanishes if and only if one symbol vanishes identically. It suffices to test the product on reproducing kernels. The proof represents the product by a two-variable entire function and transforms the equation for a left factor by $\exp(-\partial_z\partial_w)$. A Fock norm identity then permits cancellation of each nonzero factor.
item.dc:creator: Youqi Liu, Jie Qin, Sui Huang

item.title: Radial Schur multipliers on trees and quantitative Fourier--Schur separation
item.description: arXiv:2610.30832v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study ordinary and completely bounded norms of radial Schur multipliers on trees. On the homogeneous tree of countably infinite degree, we show that boundedness implies complete boundedness. The argument realizes arbitrary matrix amplifications of a shifted Toeplitz symbol inside rectangular corners of the original multiplier. It also applies to some locally finite trees of unbounded degree. Consequently, the completely bounded radial multiplier theorem of Gonz\'alez-P\'erez, Parcet, P\'erez Garc\'ia and Wang has no general counterpart with ordinary norms. We also determine the optimal order of the comparison constant for positive definite even symbols. For each $1 < p < \infty$ with $p \neq 2$, we construct radial symbols on finitely generated nonabelian free groups, supported in the ball of radius $N$, whose completely bounded Herz--Schur norms remain bounded as $N \to \infty$, whereas their ordinary Fourier multiplier norms grow at least like $N^{|1-\frac{2}{p}|}$. For each fixed $0 < \vartheta < \pi$, we also determine the exact order $t^{-|1-\frac{2}{p}|}$ of both the ordinary and completely bounded Fourier multiplier norms of the damped radial phases $s \mapsto \mathrm{e}^{(-t+\mathrm{i}\vartheta)|s|}$ as $t \to 0$. Finally, we compute the local amenability modulus of free balls, we bound the Fourier--Schur ratio of free balls from above and below in terms of this modulus, and we show that its restriction to radial symbols grows polynomially in the radius.
item.dc:creator: C\'edric Arhancet

item.title: An elementary proof of rational injectivity in equivariant KK-theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.31174v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Antonini, Azzali and Skandalis proved that, for every countable discrete group $\Gamma$, the canonical map $E\Gamma\to\underline{E}\Gamma$ induces a split injection in equivariant $KK$-theory with real coefficients. In this paper, we give a more elementary proof of the corresponding rational injectivity result in ordinary equivariant $KK$-theory without using $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors.
item.dc:creator: Denghui Luo, Geng Tian

item.title: Chaos of Caputo derivative
item.description: arXiv:2610.31255v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study bounded realizations of Caputo differentiation on coefficient Banach spaces of fractional power series. The main contribution is an explicit quantitative analysis of local approximation and periodic reconstruction. We determine the least possible simultaneous error in the initial displacement and the prescribed target. The optimal value is attained, and a minimizing perturbation is given explicitly. We also solve the exact-arrival problem and establish uniqueness of its least-norm solution. These formulas provide computable approximation times and identify the sharp threshold for hypercyclicity, mixing and Devaney chaos. Every periodic point is described by a finite block whose geometric repetition yields exact norm formulas. The resulting approximations attain any prescribed sufficiently large minimal period near any given vector. For distinct positive powers, a simultaneous block construction gives quantitative error estimates and the same sharp threshold for disjoint mixing. Compact embeddings relate the Banach realizations to the Mittag-Leffler-Caputo Fr\'echet space. They also exhibit dense stable invariant subspaces inside chaotic realizations. The local approximation condition is a norm formulation of classical transitivity. Its quantitative evaluation, together with explicit periodic and simultaneous reconstruction, provides the central results of the study.
item.dc:creator: El-Mahdi Nafia, Aziz El Ghazouani, M'hamed El Omari

item.title: Ultraproducts of crossed product C*algebras
item.description: arXiv:2505.11871v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the relationship between the ultraproduct of a crossed product C*algebra $(A\rtimes_{r}G)^{\omega}$ and the crossed product of an ultraproduct C*algebra $A^{\omega}\rtimes _{r}G$ for a fixed free ultrafilter $\omega$ on $\mathbb{N}$.
item.dc:creator: Zhengyu Fu

item.title: Remarks on Derivations on Maximal Triangular Operator Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2508.07347v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This note concerns bounded derivations on maximal triangular operator algebras on a Hilbert space. Given any bounded derivation $\delta$ on a maximal triangular algebra whose invariant lattice is continuous at 1, an operator which is shown to implement $\delta$ is constructed explicitly. For a general reducible maximal triangular algebra the same construction yields an operator which is shown to implement any $\delta$, if and only if $\delta$ obeys an additional triple product rule. This work is based on unpublished parts of the author's dissertation [19] and describes a variant of the proof of a more general result in [21] and is thus in effect a footnote to that work. To the best of the author's knowledge the constructive proof and triple product rule have not appeared elsewhere. The work here is not set in the context of the large body of subsequent research, and no claims are made regarding its relationship to later developments.
item.dc:creator: Mark Spivack

item.title: Integral representations of quantum R\'enyi divergences on von Neumann algebras
item.description: arXiv:2608.21214v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove an integral representation of the $\alpha$-$z$ R\'enyi divergences for normal states on arbitrary von Neumann algebras. Along each ray $z=c\alpha$, the divergence is a positive average of relative entropies evaluated in a canonical family of escort states. For orders $\alpha$ above one, we require the divergence to be finite, whereas for orders below one support inclusion suffices. An explicit boundary correction removes the lower-order support assumption. The proof uses a compatible weighted Haagerup $L^p$ scale and applies outside the data-processing region. For faithful density matrices, we express the derivative of the escort relative entropy with respect to the R\'enyi order in terms of a nonnegative fluctuation quantity. Differences of order-one derivatives of the divergence give quantum Fisher information and Wigner-Yanase skew information. For faithful bipartite density matrices, we also express optimized conditional $\alpha$-$z$ entropies at orders above one as averages of ordinary conditional entropies. Further applications concern coherent-state divergences in quantum field theory and the optimizing order for the strong converse exponent in hypothesis-testing.
item.dc:creator: Tanay Kibe, Pratik Roy

item.title: Facets of nondegeneracy: central type factor groups, Heisenberg representations and Hadamard matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.11785v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a pair of complementary subgroups $P$ and $N$ of a finite group $G$, we first discuss how the same type of functions $\mathbb E\colon P\times N\to \mathbb T$, which we call bi-$1$-cocycles, appear naturally in the study of projective representations of $G$ of Heisenberg type and second cohomology of $G$ and of its dual quantum group $\widehat G$. We show then that such representations are irreducible and the corresponding ordinary and dual $2$-cocycles are nondegenerate if and only if the matrix $(\mathbb E(p,n))_{p,n}$ is invertible, if and only if it is Hadamard. We illustrate the result with examples arising from symplectic nilpotent Lie algebras over finite fields with two complementary Lagrangian subalgebras.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Bieliavsky, Victor Gayral, Sergey Neshveyev, Lars Tuset
